_comment: Registry of real, reputable captures that exercise the advanced-threat engines in app/advanced_engines.py. Every entry names a signal family, its origin, a direct URL, an sha256 of the FETCHED artifact (pre-extraction for .zip / .gz), and expected_signals reflecting what actually fired when the engines were run against the file - NOT what the source page claims. `commit` files live at pcaps/<file>; `fetch` files download to _cache/<file> via fetch.py and are gitignored.

captures.notes: 622 pkts. Single MAC 00:07:0d:af:f4:54 announces 9 distinct IPv4 addresses in ARP requests - textbook arp_mac_many_ips.
438 pkts. iodine over pirate.sea - 222 unique subdomains, uniq_ratio=1.00, max entropy 5.74, mean label length 47.

captures.source: Johannes Weber - The Ultimate PCAP (listed on wireshark.org Resources)
captures.sha256_note: sha256 is of the fetched .gz artifact, verified before decompression
captures.notes: 51k pkts. Fires FOUR distinct advanced signals in one capture. 6 DHCP servers offer leases (rogue_dhcp), 3 MACs claim 192.168.42.1 (arp_ip_multi_mac), a Raspberry Pi MAC announces 4 IPs (arp_mac_many_ips), and 47 NXDOMAIN responses to one host (nxdomain_storm).

captures.source: Stratosphere IPS / Malware Capture Facility Project, CTU University Prague (Sebastian Garcia)
captures.notes: 199k pkts. Conficker botnet capture. NXDOMAIN storm (155 failed lookups on one host) is the primary DGA symptom the engine catches; the dga_domain engine itself did not fire because Conficker's 8-char labels have vowel ratio >= 0.25, above the current threshold - a known engine limitation, not a test failure. Also produces beaconing (median 5s intervals) and rogue_dhcp as bonus signals.

captures.sha256_note: sha256 is of the fetched .zip artifact, verified before extraction. The extracted .pcap sha256 is 09721b1e3203d78aeb282f0012e2f6d0959c65e8c1a9399e43912c640bfbc7e1.
captures.notes: 15k pkts. Real Cobalt Strike C2 traffic. sni_ip_mismatch fires 5x (SNIs like a.docusign.com resolving to AWS ranges - possible domain fronting). Beaconing did NOT fire: this Hancitor C2 is HTTP over port 80, not TCP-SYN periodic, so it falls outside the beaconing engine's TCP-start filter. Documented gap - not a test failure.
